name: Opportunity Rover
goal: Search for geological evidence of ancient liquid water and assess past Martian habitability.
alt: The Opportunity rover: a gold-coloured body with a solar deck, a tall camera mast and six wheels.

hotspots.label: Panoramic camera
hotspots.description: Twin cameras on the mast that took the wide pictures of Mars.

hotspots.label: Robotic arm
hotspots.description: Holds the tools that touch and study rocks up close.

hotspots.label: Six wheels
hotspots.description: Each wheel has its own motor, and the suspension helps the rover roll over small rocks.

story: Landed on Mars in 2004 for a planned 90-day mission, Opportunity explored the Red Planet for over 15 years, traveling approximately 28 miles. It discovered hematite-rich spherules and gypsum veins, providing strong geological evidence that liquid water once existed on Mars. A planet-wide dust storm in 2018 reduced its solar power, and NASA declared the mission complete in February 2019.

evidence.text: Opportunity discovered hematite-rich spherules and gypsum veins, providing geological evidence of past liquid water on Mars.
evidence.label: confirmed

evidence.text: Meridiani Planum experienced aqueous environmental conditions that may have been suitable for ancient microbial life.
evidence.label: interpretation

evidence.text: Whether any ancient Martian watery environment actually harbored microscopic life or preserved organic biosignatures remains unknown.
evidence.label: unknown

legacy: Drove approximately 45.16 km (28.06 miles) across Mars and revealed strong geological evidence that liquid water once existed on the planet.

openQuestion.prompt: Opportunity revealed that Mars once had liquid water. What should a future rover search for next?
choices: Preserved organic biosignatures of ancient microbial life
How the Martian atmosphere and surface water disappeared over time
Geological rock layers in an unexplored crater basin

name: Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV)
goal: Provide mobility for Apollo astronauts on the lunar surface to extend exploration range and sample collection.
alt: A simplified model of the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle: an open frame with four wire-mesh wheels, two seats and an umbrella-shaped antenna.

hotspots.label: Umbrella antenna
hotspots.description: Pointed at Earth to send TV pictures and radio from the Moon.

hotspots.label: TV camera
hotspots.description: Sent live pictures of the astronauts at work back to Earth.

hotspots.label: Hand controller
hotspots.description: One T-shaped handle between the seats steered and drove the rover.

hotspots.label: Wire-mesh wheels
hotspots.description: Woven wire tyres with metal treads gripped the dusty Moon ground and kept the weight down.

story: The Lunar Roving Vehicle was used on Apollo 15, 16, and 17, allowing astronauts to travel farther across the lunar surface and collect more geological samples. The three rovers covered approximately 90.4 km in total: 27.8 km on Apollo 15, 26.7 km on Apollo 16, and 35.9 km on Apollo 17. The vehicles remain on the Moon at their respective landing sites.

evidence.text: Three Lunar Roving Vehicles were driven on the Moon during Apollo 15, Apollo 16, and Apollo 17, extending astronaut traverse range.
evidence.label: confirmed

evidence.text: The LRV increased the amount of lunar terrain astronauts could explore and the geological samples they could collect.
evidence.label: interpretation

evidence.text: The long-term effects of decades of lunar temperature cycles, radiation, and micrometeorite impacts on the parked vehicles remain difficult to assess directly.
evidence.label: unknown

legacy: Enabled extended crewed mobility on the Moon, covering approximately 90.4 km across Apollo 15, 16, and 17.

openQuestion.prompt: The LRVs sit silently on the Moon. What key lesson should future lunar rovers take from their design?
choices: Dust-resistant mesh wheel designs for fine lunar regolith
High-efficiency solar and thermal battery management
Autonomous navigation for tele-operated surface scouting

name: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter
goal: Demonstrate powered, controlled flight in the extremely thin Martian atmosphere.
alt: The Ingenuity helicopter: a small box body with two rotors stacked above it, a solar panel on top and four legs.

hotspots.label: Two rotors
hotspots.description: Spin in opposite directions, very fast, because the air on Mars is so thin.

hotspots.label: Solar panel
hotspots.description: Charged the battery that kept the helicopter warm at night.

hotspots.label: Landing legs
hotspots.description: Four legs that cushioned each landing.

payload: Solar Array and Lithium-Ion Battery Pack
story: Arriving on Mars in 2021, Ingenuity achieved the first powered flight on another world, marking a historic milestone in aviation. Originally designed for a 30-day demonstration involving five flights, it completed 72 flights over nearly three years, serving as an aerial scout for Perseverance before rotor blade damage ended flight operations in January 2024.

evidence.text: Ingenuity completed 72 powered flights, covering approximately 17 km and reaching altitudes of up to 24 meters in the thin Martian atmosphere.
evidence.label: confirmed

evidence.text: Aerial scouting can support rover exploration by identifying safer driving routes and scientifically interesting geological targets.
evidence.label: interpretation

evidence.text: How future multi-rotor aerial vehicles will navigate Martian dust storms and carry heavier scientific instruments.
evidence.label: unknown

legacy: Demonstrated that powered aerodynamic flight is possible on Mars, establishing a new dimension of aerial planetary exploration.

openQuestion.prompt: Ingenuity proved aerial exploration works on Mars. What capability should next-generation Mars helicopters possess?
choices: Mapping subsurface water ice deposits from low flight altitudes
Transporting geological rock samples across steep crater walls
Scouting unmapped Martian lava tubes and subsurface caves
